deep.reconstruction:
The page holds only a numerical table. There are no derivations. It continues folio 22 and runs on into folio 24. Each half of the page has five columns: A | B | ΔB | C = A + B | ΔC. The argument A runs from 1.120 to 1.160 (left half) and from 1.160 to 1.200 (right half), in steps of 0.001.

Identification (mine, verified numerically): B(A) = log10(1 + 10^(-A)), rounded to 5 decimals. This is Gauss's addition logarithm. Spot checks:
- A = 1.12: 10^-1.12 = 0.075858, so log10(1.075858) = 0.031755, giving 0.03175.
- A = 1.15: 0.0297062, giving 0.02971.
- A = 1.16: 0.029052, giving 0.02905.
- A = 1.18: 0.027786, giving 0.02779.
- A = 1.20: 0.026572, giving 0.02657.

The fourth column is C = A + B, i.e. C = log10(1 + 10^A) in the form Gauss tabulated. Examples: 1.120 + 0.03175 = 1.15175, and 1.200 + 0.02657 = 1.22657.

The difference columns are first differences of B and C in units of the fifth decimal:
- ΔB is 7 or 6. This matches dB/dA = -10^-A/(1+10^-A) ≈ -0.066, i.e. about 6.6 units per step.
- ΔC = 100 − |ΔB|, so 93 or 94.

Purpose: with such a table, log(a + b) follows from log a and log b. Set A = log a − log b. Then log(a + b) = log a + B, equivalently log b + C. This avoids taking antilogarithms. It is the content of Gauss's five-place table of 'Gaussian logarithms', published 1812.

The pattern of differences shifts from 8/92 (folio 22) to 7/93 and 6/94 (this folio) and on to 5/95 (folio 24). This is consistent with the slowly decreasing derivative.
errors: No computational errors found in the spot checks.
Every C = A + B entry and every pair of difference columns is internally consistent: consecutive B differences match ΔB, and ΔB + ΔC = 100.

Borderline rounding at A = 1.127: the exact value is B = 0.0312650 (to 7 places), and Gauss writes 0.03126. This is acceptable given the rounding of an exact half in the 6th place, or a final digit that is barely below .5.

results.what: Five-place table of B(A) = log10(1 + 10^-A) and C = A + B, with first differences, for A = 1.120 to 1.200
results.modern_name: Gaussian (addition/subtraction) logarithms; log-sum-exp table in base 10
results.usually_credited_to: Concept: Z. Leonelli (1802/1803). Popular five-place table: C. F. Gauss, Monatliche Correspondenz 26 (1812).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a manuscript sheet of Gauss's well-known table of addition logarithms, published 1812. That fits the 1809–1812 'Kleine Aufsätze' bundle. The function and Gauss's authorship of such a table are standard history. Only the manuscript working form is of minor archival interest.

checkable.asserts: Approximately 0.0312650. This is the borderline case for the entry 0.03126 at A = 1.127.
The derivative implies a ΔB of about 6.5 units of the 5th decimal per step 0.001, consistent with the tabulated differences of 6 and 7.

transcription_corrections: The arguments 1,131, 1,141 and 1,151 appear in the image with an ink blot on the last digit ('1,13●', '1,14●', '1,15●'). The values 1,131, 1,141 and 1,151 are confirmed by sequence and by the B values.
The difference columns are written between rows in the original. The transcription's attachment of each difference to the preceding row is correct.
There is a faint stray stroke ('/') in the header cell above the right half. It carries no content.
The partial column visible at the left edge is the C-difference column (92/93) of folio 22, bleeding into the photograph. It is not part of folio 23.
